prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The invention relates to a two-wheeled vehicle frame with two frame half-shells (1, 1′) which are joined so as to form a support frame (3), thereby forming at least one inner cavity (2). The support frame (3) has at least one separating surface (4) on which the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) rest against each other. The support frame (3) preferably has receiving areas (5, 6, 7) for a handlebar tube and/or a bottom bracket and/or an operator seat tube. The support frame (3) forms a rear structure (8) for assembling a rear wheel (9) at the rear end when seen in the travel direction (z). In order to form the rear structure (8), a left-hand support brace (10) when seen in the travel direction (z) and a right-hand support brace (11) when seen in the travel direction (z) are provided such that the rear wheel (8) can be mounted between the two support braces (10, 11). According to the invention, the separating surface (4) runs between the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) as well as through the left-hand support brace (10) and through the right-hand support brace (11).

outputs.L1: The invention relates to a two-wheeled vehicle frame comprising two frame half-shells (1, 1′) joined together to form a support frame (3) and thereby define at least one inner cavity (2). The support frame (3) has at least one separating surface (4) along which the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) abut each other. Preferably, the support frame (3) includes receiving areas (5, 6, 7) for a handlebar tube, a bottom bracket, and/or an operator seat tube. At its rear end, viewed in the direction of travel (z), the support frame (3) forms a rear structure (8) for mounting a rear wheel (9). To form the rear structure (8), a left-hand support brace (10) and a right-hand support brace (11), as viewed in the direction of travel (z), are provided such that the rear wheel (9) can be mounted between them. According to the invention, the separating surface (4) extends between the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) and through both the left-hand support brace (10) and the right-hand support brace (11).
outputs.L2:
The invention concerns a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle that is constructed from two frame half-shells (1, 1′). These half-shells are connected to create a load-bearing frame (3) containing at least one internal cavity (2). The two half-shells (1, 1′) adjoin along at least one parting surface (4) of the load-bearing frame (3). Preferably, the frame (3) includes mounting regions (5, 6, 7) for one or more of the following components: a handlebar tube, a bottom bracket, and a rider-seat tube.

Viewed in the direction of travel (z), the load-bearing frame (3) incorporates a rear assembly (8) at its rear end for mounting a rear wheel (9). This rear assembly (8) includes a left support strut (10) and a right support strut (11), defined relative to the direction of travel (z), with the rear wheel positioned between them. In accordance with the invention, the parting surface (4) extends between the two frame half-shells (1, 1′) and continues through both the left and right support struts (10, 11).
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a frame for a two-wheeled vehicle, such as a bicycle or motorcycle. The frame is formed from two frame half-shells that are joined together to create a load-bearing support frame having at least one internal cavity.

The support frame includes at least one separating surface along which the two frame half-shells contact and rest against one another. The frame preferably further comprises receiving areas configured to accommodate one or more vehicle components, including a handlebar tube, a bottom bracket, and an operator seat tube.

A rear structure of the frame comprises a left-hand support brace and a right-hand support brace. These braces are spaced apart so that a rear wheel can be mounted between them. The separating surface between the two frame half-shells extends through both the left-hand support brace and the right-hand support brace, such that the braces form part of the joined half-shell construction.
outputs.L4:
A frame for a two-wheeled vehicle is constructed from first and second half-shells that are joined along a separating surface. When assembled, the half-shells define a hollow, load-bearing support frame having one or more receiving regions for accommodating vehicle components, such as a drive unit, an energy-storage device, or other functional assemblies. The frame further includes left and right support braces extending rearward from the main support-frame region and configured to support or mount a rear wheel.

The separating surface between the two half-shells extends continuously through both the left and right rear support braces. Accordingly, the main frame and the rear wheel-supporting structure can be formed as portions of the same two half-shells and joined in a common assembly operation. This integrated shell construction reduces the number of separate structural components and joining points, while providing a lightweight, rigid frame with enclosed cavities and defined component-receiving areas.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a European patent abstract for a shell-constructed bicycle frame in which two half-shells form the support frame and their joint plane passes through both the left-hand and right-hand rear-wheel support braces.
counterfactuals.output: A bicycle frame comprises first and second complementary half-shells joined along a joint plane to form a load-bearing support frame. The support frame includes a front frame portion for receiving a steering assembly, a crank region, a seat-supporting portion, and left-hand and right-hand rear-wheel support braces extending towards respective rear-wheel mounting regions. The joint plane extends through both the left-hand and the right-hand rear-wheel support braces, such that each brace is formed by corresponding portions of the two half-shells. The half-shells may be produced from fibre-reinforced composite material, metal, or plastics material and joined by adhesive bonding, welding, fastening, or combinations thereof. Forming the rear-wheel support braces across the common joint plane facilitates manufacture of the frame with a reduced number of components, while providing accurate alignment, continuous load paths, and increased torsional rigidity.
